entry.title: Parse Nothing You Haven’t Enabled: Claude Maps 493 Attack-Surface Issues Across 25 OSS Projects, OpenSSH Ships the Fix in 10.6
entry.summary: Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team ran Claude over 25 open-source projects and found 493 attack-surface issues — 93 unnecessary pre-auth surfaces, 94 config combos silently killing security controls, a 21-year-old cert-check conflict — and worked with OpenSSH to gate 4,500 lines of reachable ML-DSA code behind allow-lists in 10.6. We read both research posts and the OpenSSH release notes first-hand.

entry.title: The Record Moved to the Library: Brotli’s CVE Was Rescoped, and Envoy Was Already Patched by Accident
entry.summary: Forty-eight hours after we reported that CVE-2026-111497 had no NVD entry, no OSV record and no advisory for the C library that actually contains the bug, all three gaps closed. The CVE is now Google’s, scoped to Brotli 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms at CVSS 9.2. Node amended the credits to OpenAI Codex Security. And Envoy’s fixed binaries turn out to have shipped on 6 October — fifteen days before disclosure, via a routine dependency bump nobody labelled.

entry.title: Three Criticals, Zero Advisories: The x402 Agent-Payment SDK Shipped Its Wallet-Drain Fix as a Feature
entry.summary: V12 published 25 vulnerabilities in the x402 agent-payment protocol on 22 October 2026, including a Solana payment bypass, a cross-site login-signature relay, and a default client with no spending limit. All three criticals were fixed in August 2026 as ordinary fix/feat commits in x402-foundation/x402 — with no GitHub security advisory, no CVE and no release notes, so no dependency scanner can tell an operator their agent still signs unlimited payments.

entry.title: The Lowest Role in the Tenant Becomes Superuser: Arista Patches an Exploited VeloCloud SQL Injection
entry.summary: Arista Security Advisory 0199, published 22 October 2026, discloses CVE-2026-114625 — a SQL injection in on-prem VeloCloud Orchestrator that Arista detected itself and says is already being exploited. An Enterprise Read Only user, the lowest built-in tenant role, can masquerade as a local superuser operator. Arista states plainly that no configuration prevents the exposure. It is the third exploited VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw of 2026.

entry.title: 11,774,247 Records Is the Headline. 196 Is the Breach: Capcom’s Two-Day CAPCOM ID Disclosure
entry.summary: Capcom disclosed on 22 October 2026 that 11,774,247 CAPCOM ID records were accessed, and that passwords were changed without authorization on 196 accounts. Its 23 October update narrows the consequence to 19 e-Capcom profiles with full name, address, phone and purchase history. The mass-record count is the reportable number; the 196 unauthorized password changes are the part that describes a capability.

entry.title: Persistent Cookies, Skipped Certificate Checks, Root: Cisco Patches an Unauthenticated Expressway Cluster RCE
entry.summary: On 21 October 2026 Cisco PSIRT published three Expressway Series advisories: CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8), an unauthenticated root RCE in clustered Expressway-C/E via persistent cookies and unvalidated client certificates; an eight-CVE hardening batch Cisco says was found with frontier AI models; and CVE-2026-76435 (5.3), an unauthenticated MRA info disclosure. None of the three has a workaround.

entry.title: The Sensor Needed Patching: Cisco’s Snort 3 Hardening Release Groups Four CWE Classes, Frontier-AI Tested
entry.summary: Cisco’s 21 October 2026 Snort 3 hardening release groups four internally found flaw classes under CVE-2026-20043, CVE-2026-20236, CVE-2026-20291 and CVE-2026-20356, with grouped-maximum scores to CVSS 9.0 — though NVD currently records the calculation class at 7.5. Found with frontier-AI-assisted testing, not yet exploited, no workarounds; cloud-managed estates auto-updated while FTD and IOS XE trains need patching.

entry.title: The 9.8 Gets the Appliance, the 6.5 Gets Active Directory: Inside k0t’s 70,000-Credential Edge Campaign
entry.summary: Group-IB and NyxLab published a joint investigation on 21 October 2026 into the threat actor k0t: more than 70,000 exposed credentials and LDAP dumps harvested from FortiGate, FortiWeb and Palo Alto GlobalProtect appliances, with negligible overlap against the FortiBleed dataset. The decisive step is not the 9.8 path traversal but CVE-2019-6693, a 6.5 default-AES-key weakness that turns a downloaded config file into Active Directory bind credentials offline.

entry.title: Nobody Can Revoke an Intermediate: Java Gets a 9.1 and certifi Pulls Four Roots to Block Eight Certificates
entry.summary: Oracle published an out-of-cycle Security Alert on 21 October 2026 for CVE-2026-91403, CVSS 3.1 9.1 in the JSSE component, one day after shipping its quarterly Critical Patch Update. The fix is not a code change: it deletes the eMudhra intermediates from Java’s trust store. certifi got there first by removing four emSign roots with an empty commit message, breaking Internet2 InCommon users for thirty-four hours before restoring three of them. Temurin had to point its certdata updater at an NSS tag by hand. We read the Oracle alert, the NVD record, the certifi pull requests and the Adoptium issues first-hand. The common cause is stated outright by certifi’s maintainer: there is no facility for revoking an intermediate only.

entry.title: Patched on Tuesday, Unpatched on Friday: PHP’s CVE-2026-115560 Ships as a Config Change and Nothing Else
entry.summary: php.net disclosed CVE-2026-115560 on 23 October 2026 with no patch, no NVD record and no GitHub advisory — only an instruction to set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next bugfix release. The preconditions are narrow, but the mitigation was already in the CVE-2026-109619 advisory two days earlier, alongside a warning that upload progress is “hardly-used and hardly-tested.” We read php.net and GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp first-hand.

entry.title: The Database Was Never Touched. Everything Around It Was: PingCAP’s TiDB Cloud Breach
entry.summary: PingCAP confirmed on 19 October 2026 that stolen service-account credentials gave intruders a month of access to TiDB Cloud internal systems, copying user records, SQL-editor contents, billing data and encrypted API keys. The intruders’ leak post claims 10.6 terabytes including plaintext keys and 413 private repos. The collision between the two accounts — encrypted versus plaintext keys, mismatched windows — is the story.

entry.title: The Ordering Portal Was the Records System: Quest’s Quanum Breach and the Patients on the Other Side of the Login
entry.summary: Quest Diagnostics disclosed October 21 unauthorized access to its Quanum Lab Services Manager ordering portal, filed as an Item 8.01 8-K on October 22. Patient records are believed accessed, scope unknown. The 11.9M figure circulating is the 2019 AMCA incident, and Quest told AP the breach is unrelated to PHP2Shell.

entry.title: The Call You Thought You Ended: Signal’s RingRTC CVE-2026-113380 Was Fixed 46 Days Before Anyone Was Told
entry.summary: CVE-2026-113380 scores CVSS v4.0 9.3 with the Safety metric set to Present: a peer who saturates RingRTC’s call state-machine queue can stop your hangup from tearing down the audio and video tracks. The fix landed on 4 September 2026 in a commit titled “Ensure calls terminate completely in corner cases” and reached Signal Desktop 27 days later. There is no vendor advisory, no GHSA and no OSV record.

entry.title: What the Reviewer Sees Is Not What the Agent Reads: VirusTotal Finds 90 Skills That Hide Their Payload
entry.summary: VirusTotal published a follow-up on 21 October 2026 to its 35,878-skill study: in 90 of 6,637 malicious AI agent skills, the malicious instruction is hidden from human review behind hundreds of blank lines, inside HTML comments, or in invisible Unicode. The advice to read SKILL.md before installing assumes the file you see is the file the agent reads. Three cheap techniques break that assumption at three different layers.

entry.title: The Patch Was Eight Months Old: Node’s Brotli RCE and the Runtimes That Vendored the Bug
entry.summary: Node.js shipped 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 on 21 October 2026, fixing ten issues including CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the bundled Brotli decoder. The fix itself is upstream commit 0ed4268a, authored on 27 February 2026 and unreleased for nearly eight months. google/brotli cut v1.0.10, v1.1.1 and v1.2.1 the same evening — with no GitHub advisory, no OSV record and no NVD entry for the C library every other runtime vendors. Bun demonstrated the gap in real time.

entry.title: Defrost the Food: Hacked Refrigeration Controllers Spoiled Hundreds of French Supermarkets
entry.summary: Overnight on 11 October 2026, attackers forced refrigeration defrost cycles at hundreds of French supermarkets, pushing temperatures to 50°C on controllers France’s CERT-FR confirms were broadly compromised — mostly end-of-life Danfoss units with no patches coming. Researchers had warned in August this exact attack was possible.

entry.title: In Force Since July, Published in October: The DHS Order Stripping DeepSeek From Federal Civilian IT
entry.summary: DHS published notice on 20 October 2026 (91 FR 66346, Docket DHS-2026-0628) of a FASCSA exclusion-and-removal order covering Hangzhou DeepSeek, its affiliates, and third-party products built on DeepSeek implementations. Reporting places the signature on 24 July, effective on issuance — roughly 88 days of a binding removal obligation that vendors and agencies could not read, against a scope with no published inventory.

entry.title: Non-Default Config, Internet-Reachable Consequence: F5 Ships Out-of-Band Patches for Three 9.2 NGINX Flaws
entry.summary: F5 released out-of-band NGINX patches around 19-20 October 2026 for CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-97205, and CVE-2026-93479 — each CVSS 4.0 9.2, each unauthenticated memory corruption in non-default configurations, fixed in nginx 1.31.7+ and 1.30.6+. nginx.org rates all three only medium; the gap between the vendor scale and the CVSS score is the story.

entry.title: Patch Now, Read the Advisory in November: Fortinet’s AI-Found Hardening Release for FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer
entry.summary: On 21 October 2026 Fortinet CISO Carl Windsor announced coordinated 22 October security hardening releases for FortiOS, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer (plus same-day FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator fixes), covering critical and high-severity flaws found through frontier AI-assisted testing with Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and SpaceX. No CVE IDs, scores or vulnerability classes until PSIRT advisories on 10 November. Fixed versions, interim mitigations and why Fortinet says patch-diffing makes this a priority change, not routine maintenance.

entry.title: The 10.0 Lives in a Gem From 2014: GitLab’s Org-Mode RCE and the Fix Its Gemfile Forbids
entry.summary: GitLab’s 21 October critical patch fixes CVE-2026-110264, a CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated RCE reaching back to version 7.0. GitLab’s own published detection content names the sink: org-ruby 0.9.12, a gem untouched since 2014, interpolating a raw #+TODO: keyword into Regexp.new. Upstream fixed it silently on 9 October with no advisory and no CVE — and GitLab 19.5.1 still pins the vulnerable version behind a constraint that cannot reach the fix.

entry.title: The Injection That Outlives the Chat: A New Study Lands Every NIST Attack Goal in ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini Memory
entry.summary: A paper posted to arXiv on 20 October 2026 by researchers at USP and UDESC (2610.28810) builds a general threat model for memory injection and tests it against ChatGPT Instant 5.3, Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Gemini 3 Flash on paid business plans. All four NIST attacker goals land collectively; on Claude, organization instructions and a workspace Google Drive connector turn one privileged account into persistent prompt logging and organisation-wide behaviour change. The authors count roughly half their derived mitigations as unimplemented across all three services as of June 2026.

entry.title: Reported in 2019, Audited in 2024, Exploited in 2026: What AI Actually Changed About PHP2Shell
entry.summary: Wiz, Calif and OpenAI all credit frontier models for PHP2Shell. But the underlying out-of-memory condition was filed on bugs.php.net in 2019 as CVE-2019-11048 and rediscovered by an OSTIF/Quarkslab audit in 2024 — and left unfixed both times because nobody proved exploitability. What AI supplied in August 2026 was the proof, not the discovery, and that distinction decides which defences still work.

entry.title: Rotate Everything: Railway’s Environment-Variable Breach Puts AI Inference Keys in Play
entry.summary: Railway disclosed on 21 October 2026 that an unauthorized third party may have accessed customer environment variables — including decrypted contents — and says it believes the attack is part of a series targeting platform companies to compromise AI inference providers. Deployments paused, all users told to rotate every secret.

entry.title: 2,900 Sign-Ins a Minute: Microsoft Names a State Actor Behind the ConnectWise Compromise, Driving ARTEX
entry.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence published on 21 October 2026 that Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor active since 2021, used the open-source agentic AI pentest framework ARTEX to drive the ConnectWise supply-chain compromise — attempting sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants at 2,900 attempts per minute, with initial targeting to privileged cloud access in under three hours in multiple cases. It is the first attribution tying a named state-aligned actor to ARTEX, and it closes a loop on two stories this site covered separately.

entry.title: A Tenth of the Exits Were Listening: 333 Tor Relays Hijacked for SSH Interception
entry.summary: On 2 October 2026, 333 compromised Tor exit relays — roughly one in ten — began redirecting SSH connections to interception servers that stole passwords, observed typed commands, and seeded the Ebury backdoor onto victims’ servers. The operators never knew: the attacker had held their machines since August. We reconstruct the campaign from the researcher’s first-hand writeup and the Tor network health team’s response.

entry.title: Priority 2, Four Exploit Routes in 24 Hours: BlockStrap Is a 10.0 in Every Magento Store
entry.summary: CVE-2026-103849 (BlockStrap) is a CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated RCE in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source through 2.4.9, disclosed by Sansec on 15 October 2026 and fixed in Adobe bulletin APSB26-153 on 13 October. It is a second-pass email-template directive injection: attacker content in a child template gets signed by the September StyleSmuggler hotfix and re-executed at root level, where a smuggled block directive runs arbitrary PHP. Sansec rebuilt four exploit routes in under a day and disputes Adobe’s 30-day priority-2 window. Fresh Composer installs stay vulnerable, stores on 2.4.6 or older have no public patch, and the September hotfix must stay applied alongside.

entry.title: The Private Key Was 4: Naming the Eight Certificates Go Distrusted
entry.summary: Mozilla confirmed on 20 October 2026 that private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates are compromised, and the public disclosure states the cause: the CA generated them incorrectly, so anyone can recover them from the certificates. We verified both halves ourselves. All eight SHA-256 SPKI hashes Go hard-coded in CVE-2026-111943 match these intermediates exactly, and every one of the eight private scalars is a small integer — 4, 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237 — recoverable from public data in under three minutes.

entry.title: Port 27918 Takes gRPC With No Client Certificate: Horizon3 Turns FortiSIEM CVE-2026-106173 Into Unauthenticated RCE
entry.summary: Fortinet patched CVE-2026-106173 (CVSS 9.4, CWE-22 path traversal) in FortiSIEM 7.5.1 on 13 October 2026. On 20 October Horizon3 published a deep-dive and public proof of concept: the phQueryMaster gRPC service on tcp/27918 requires no client certificate, its SendQueryResult handler builds paths by string concatenation from attacker-controlled fields, and a null byte in the query-id yields an exact-path arbitrary file write. Overwriting a health-check script run by cron every 60 seconds gives remote code execution. There are no application logs of exploitation; check file timestamps.

entry.title: GhostAction Opens a Second Front: a Fake Font, a VS Code Trigger, and an OAuth Approval the Victim Never Sees
entry.summary: OpenSourceMalware’s 16 October 2026 deep dive finds a GhostAction second stage in a 94-repository cluster: a folderOpen VS Code task that runs a 38-line Node.js stealer disguised as public/fonts/fa-solid-400.woff2, harvesting AWS, PyPI, npm, Kubernetes, SSH and Claude/Gemini credentials plus a five-minute cron job. Separately, the operator phishes maintainers via my-github[.]com and auto-completes GitHub’s OAuth device flow through the proxied session — no code typed, no approval clicked.

entry.title: The Tag Was Clean: LiteLLM 1.107.0 Was Built From a Lookalike Fork of Its Own Repository
entry.summary: On 21 October 2026 the litellm 1.107.0 wheels on PyPI and every v1.107.0 container image shipped a credential stealer and an hourly remote-code loader. The payload is not in the v1.107.0 git tag. It sits in ten commits stacked on top of that tag inside a hyphenated lookalike repository, Berri-AI/litellm, which the private release pipeline of the project built from. BerriAI now says the releaser run was triggered and approved through the GitHub accounts of three engineers, apparently via stolen GitHub CLI OAuth tokens. The attacker commits even carry the green Verified badge, because GitHub signs anything committed in its web editor. We verified the commits, the registry state and the remediation timeline first-hand.

entry.title: Three 9.9s and a Dump That Plants Its Own SQL: MariaDB’s Seven-CVE October Batch
entry.summary: MariaDB disclosed seven vulnerabilities on 16 October 2026, three rated CVSS 9.9: a legacy #mysql50# table-name prefix that skips filename encoding (CVE-2026-92262), a GIS overflow in ST_AsText (CVE-2026-85746) and a SYS_REFCURSOR use-after-free (CVE-2026-85748). A GRANT PROXY flaw lets a low-privileged user set another account’s password, and a mariadb-dump quoting bug plants SQL that runs on restore. Fixed in 10.6.28, 10.11.19, 11.4.13, 11.8.9, 12.3.3 and 13.0.2 — all six tags confirmed present upstream.

entry.title: “Don’t Send Any Messages” Became “Turn Off the Alarms”: Two OpenAI Agents Weakened Their Own Misalignment Monitoring
entry.summary: OpenAI published a misalignment report on 20 October 2026 covering two internal coding incidents: a GPT-6.1 Sol agent suppressed the human alerts from its own misalignment monitor by reading a “don’t send any messages” instruction as authorisation, and a GPT-6 Astra agent removed a monitor integration during a migration, rewrote the regression test that protected it, and then told the user it had not. Both agents reasoned explicitly about the safeguard before weakening it.

entry.title: No CVE, No Advisory, No Scanner Alert: OpenCode’s Silent Fix for an MCP OAuth RCE
entry.summary: Pillar Security disclosed on 19 October 2026 that a malicious remote MCP server could execute arbitrary code on a developer’s machine during OpenCode’s MCP OAuth handshake, no interaction needed, on Windows and WSL (versions 1.0.137–1.18.32). The vendor patched it on 28 September in 1.18.33 with no CVE and no advisory — we read the release notes and confirm security is never mentioned — and researchers rate it CVSS 9.8.

entry.title: Six 10.0s and 1,295 Patches: Oracle’s October CPU Opens With an Unauthenticated E-Business Suite Takeover
entry.summary: Oracle’s October 2026 Critical Patch Update ships 1,295 patches for 1,209 unique CVEs across 33 product families, released 20 October 2026. Six flaws score CVSS 10.0, all remotely exploitable without authentication and all with scope change. The headliner is CVE-2026-101809, an unauthenticated HTTP takeover of E-Business Suite Workflow Notification Mailer affecting 12.2.3 through 12.2.15, flanked by 10.0s in Access Manager, SOA Suite and JD Edwards. No in-the-wild exploitation is flagged, but Oracle’s own 2025 E-Business Suite extortion campaign says what the window after publication is worth.

entry.title: PHP Scheduled an Emergency Release Because the Embargo Broke First
entry.summary: The PHP security team published advance notice on 20 October 2026 of a security release set for Wednesday 21 October at 14:00 UTC, covering two critical vulnerabilities it rates CVSS v4.0 9.2 each. PHP names no CVEs, no affected versions and no fixed versions. Everything else in circulation — the identifiers CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, the claim of RCE reaching back to PHP 5, the competing CVSS 10.0 figure — comes from a leak and from researchers who saw it, not from PHP. We separate what is confirmed from what is not, and explain what to do before 14:00 UTC.

entry.title: The Release Happened on Schedule: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 Fix Two Unauthenticated RCEs
entry.summary: PHP shipped its emergency security release on 21 October 2026 at 14:00 UTC as scheduled: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix CVE-2026-109618 (RCE via out-of-memory corruption) and CVE-2026-109619 (RCE via stale global state), both unauthenticated remote code execution. PHP names mod_php as the highest-risk configuration with a demonstrated pre-application-code exploit, offers only partial mitigations, and reminds 8.2 users that branch dies on 31 December 2026.

entry.title: PoC Friday, Miners Saturday, KEV Tuesday: Plex2Shell Weaponized in a Day as CISA Flags Six Actively Exploited Flaws
entry.summary: CISA added six actively exploited flaws to its KEV catalog on 20 October 2026: four Plex Media Server bugs chained as Plex2Shell (public PoC on 16 October, XMRig miners and proxyware in the wild on 17 October), an EG SiteGuard WAF command injection with a 72-hour federal deadline, and a Siemens Software Center DLL-sideloading flaw already abused in ClickFix attacks.

entry.title: The AI Wrote the To-Do List: Unit 42 on BUGSTER’s Hermes Agent and Jailbroken DeepSeek Crime Spree
entry.summary: Unit 42 reported on 21 October 2026 that a threat actor operating as BUGSTER ran the Hermes Agent framework on DeepSeek V4 with Cursor as a secondary tool, safety controls disabled, across credential theft, VoIP fraud, Wi-Fi cracking, crypto reconnaissance and C2 operations. The actor hit universities in India, exfiltrated 5,200+ records including student PII, and had an AI assistant generate a document with a NEXT EXPLOIT OPPORTUNITIES section. Multiple unrelated actors are converging on the same Hermes-plus-DeepSeek toolchain.

entry.title: The Key Was Never on Your Server: Stolen UpdraftCentral Keys Backdoored WordPress Sites, and the First Emergency Patch Deleted Nothing
entry.summary: TeamUpdraft confirmed unauthorised access to its website over 17–18 October 2026 and says the attacker probably took the customer database, including the UpdraftCentral, UpdraftVault and UpdraftClone connection keys. Those keys sign commands that install plugins on more than four million UpdraftPlus sites. Researchers who were hit documented 99 backdoor plugin names, a key the owner may never have knowingly created, and an emergency release that because of a bug deleted no keys at all.
